title: The twelve (Mark 3:1–19)
hookLine: a withered hand healed, then he names twelve to be with him

cards: Twelve names, read out on a hillside. Teams usually get picked for what people can do: speed, skill, good ideas. Here, Jesus climbs a hill, calls the ones he wants, and they come.
He chooses twelve, and Mark lists every one by name. But before saying what they'll do, Mark says what they were chosen for first, and it isn't a skill.

teach.b: First, a hand. On another sabbath, in a synagogue, there's a man whose hand is withered, and people watch to see what Jesus will do.
He asks them, in the Douay-Rheims: "Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy?" Nobody answers.
Mark says Jesus looked round at them with anger, grieved, the Douay says, for the blindness of their hearts. Then he says to the man: stretch forth thy hand. And it's restored.
Jesus goes up a mountain and calls those he wants, and they come. "And he made that twelve should be with him, and that he might send them to preach."
Some readers hear in the number the twelve tribes of Israel, a people being gathered again. Third, the order.
First, to be with him. Then, to be sent. Before any preaching or healing, the job is to be with him: walk the roads, eat at the same fire, watch him pray at dawn.
Fourth, the names. Simon, whom he names Peter.

teach.h: SONS OF THUNDER, AND A BETRAYER.
teach.b: James and John, whom he nicknames sons of thunder. Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddeus, Simon the Cananean, and Judas Iscariot, who, Mark says right away, would betray him.
Fishermen you've already met, two brothers nicknamed for thunder, and one named, right in the list, as the betrayer. Apostle is Greek, apostolos, one who is sent.

teach.h: THAT TWELVE SHOULD BE WITH HIM.
teach.b: Catholics believe the bishops today are the apostles' successors, a line that runs, they say, all the way back to that hill.

how: Catholics keep feast days for each of the apostles through the year, and profess in the Creed that the Church is apostolic, led by bishops understood as the apostles' successors.

o: a student who stays home to study
a hermit who never leaves his cave
one who is sent out with a message

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: the twelve were chosen first to preach
first "that twelve should be with him," then to be sent to preach.
Mark names Judas as the betrayer in the list of twelve
he tells us right away that Judas would betray him.
Jesus nicknamed two brothers sons of thunder
James and John, the sons of Zebedee.

games.q: you've just been chosen as one of the twelve. what's the first thing Mark says you're chosen for?
games.why: "that twelve should be with him, and that he might send them to preach." being with him comes first.

practice: Think of the people you really walk through life with, the ones you'd call when everything goes wrong, the ones who've watched you at your worst, and let their names come one at a time; you may not get to twelve, and that's fine.
If you can, write them down. If you pray, hold each name before God for a moment; if you don't, just be grateful, one name at a time.

wordCard.voice: Apostle. From the Greek apostolos, one who is sent. But in Mark, the twelve are called first to be with him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: one who is sent, a messenger with a mission.

carryVoice: Your line: first, to be with him. Being with him came before any doing. Day one hundred ninety-nine, in the books.
